% Layout fixture: Beamer two-column frames and a table with maths. Written for
% ReadableSTEM's tests (MIT); no third-party text.
\documentclass{beamer}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\setbeamertemplate{navigation symbols}{}
\setbeamertemplate{footline}[frame number]

\begin{document}

\begin{frame}{Two Views of a Spring}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      Force view
      \begin{itemize}
        \item Hooke's law: $F = -k x$.
        \item The force points to the origin.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      Energy view
      \begin{itemize}
        \item Stored energy: $U = \tfrac{1}{2} k x^2$.
        \item The energy is zero at $x = 0$.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Measured Quantities}
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{lcc}
    Quantity & Symbol & Value \\
    \hline
    Mass & $m$ & $0.50$ kg \\
    Stiffness & $k$ & $8.0$ N/m \\
    Frequency & $\omega = \sqrt{k/m}$ & $4.0$ rad/s \\
    Period & $T = 2\pi/\omega$ & $1.57$ s \\
  \end{tabular}
\end{frame}

\end{document}
